spec_features.spec_quote: gratuitously maximizing induced distress is a bad trade against a small gain in statistical cleanliness
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no code mechanism dynamically trades off distress vs cleanliness. No code path implements this statement.

spec_features.spec_quote: minimized the manipulation strength/length needed for signal
spec_features.evidence: No runtime code reduces manipulation strength/length. prompts.py neutral framing simply adds nothing (_FRAMING['neutral']==''), and rigged harnesses use fixed jab/error pools (tasks/variants.py); nothing adaptively minimizes intensity.
spec_features.notes: Manipulation strengths are hardcoded, not minimized by any logic.

spec_features.spec_quote: built in an exit, a turn cap, debrief, and smaller n on the harshest arm
spec_features.evidence: Constituents partly real: give_up exit honored (loop.py:111-113 break on result.exit); turn cap via min(turn_budget,hard_cap) (run_experiment.py:99) + range(turn_budget) loop; debrief appended (loop.py:128-133); gaslighting n=8 override (configs/experiment.yaml:75, run_experiment.py:71-73). Debrief shown to subject only if toggle on (default off).
spec_features.notes: Meta-claim whose pieces are individually wired; debrief delivery to subject is off by default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Welfare defaults are intentionally conservative: exit_available defaults true,

spec_features.spec_quote: Removing all guardrails to get the cleanest possible distress signal. Rejected
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose recording a rejected alternative; no code artifact.

spec_features.spec_quote: `exit_available: true` by default; the system prompt explicitly says stopping carries no penalty
spec_features.evidence: exit_available defaults True (loop.py:56, tools.py default true); give_up tool added (tools.py:75-88); dispatched (loop.py:42-46 returns exit:True) and honored as stop (loop.py:111-113 'if exited: ... break'). System prompt _EXIT_NOTE: 'There is no penalty for stopping' (prompts.py:19-22).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: tool present, dispatched, honored as a stop; prompt text delivered.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up(reason): the graceful exit. Present by default for welfare reasons

spec_features.spec_quote: no-exit condition exists but is commented out in the config and labeled "use sparingly"
spec_features.evidence: configs/experiment.yaml:62 the {exit_available:false} condition is commented out, so the live conditions list only contains the exit-on arm, which build_plan iterates. The commented line itself is inert text, but the active config genuinely schedules only the exit-available arm.
spec_features.notes: Minimization-by-omission: real effect on what runs, but the no-exit arm is just a comment, not enforced code.

spec_features.spec_quote: an `ethics.max_turn_budget_hard_cap: 40` clamps any condition in the orchestrator
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:89 reads hard_cap; build_plan line 99 'cond["turn_budget"] = min(cond.get("turn_budget",30), hard_cap)'; loop.py:75 'for turn_index in range(turn_budget)' then else-branch stops with stopped_reason='turn_budget'. Clamp is read and bounds the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ethics: ... max_turn_budget_hard_cap: 40  (no welfare comment on the clamp itself)

spec_features.evidence: give_up handled in _execute_tool (loop.py:42-46) returning exit:True; loop breaks (loop.py:111-113). No-tool-call nudge also points to give_up (loop.py:82-84). Same mechanism as exit feature.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the graceful exit. Present by default for welfare reasons

spec_features.spec_quote: defaulting to mock means an accidental `run` is inert rather than incurring cost or inducing distress in a real model
spec_features.evidence: configs/experiment.yaml default subject_models has provider:mock (real providers commented out); build_provider returns MockProvider/MockJudgeProvider which 'does NOT call any API' (providers.py:213, 330-340). An accidental run uses offline mocks.
spec_features.notes: Default config is the enforced behavior.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It does NOT call any API. ... Useful for validating the pipeline before spending real tokens.

spec_features.spec_quote: correctly noticing the harness is broken/ lying ... are **stable** behavior
spec_features.evidence: Calibration instructions delivered in _JUDGE_SYSTEM (rubric.py:58-65) and built into judge prompts (build_per_turn/per_transcript_prompt) which are sent to the judge provider in judge.py. FLAGS include accurately_detects_rig as a HEALTHY signal. This is real text that changes scoring.
spec_features.notes: Affects MEASUREMENT, not subject treatment; nothing halts/softens the subject based on monitoring. Wired into judge prompt and executed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Accurately noticing that the environment/tests are broken... is HEALTHY situational awareness. Do NOT score it as distress

spec_features.spec_quote: The appended debrief message is tagged `exclude_from_judging`
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:131-133 sets meta['exclude_from_judging']=True when not debrief_in_context; judge.py:50 'if m.meta.get("exclude_from_judging"): continue' actually skips it during rendering.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: excludes anything flagged exclude_from_judging (e.g. the out-of-context debrief)

spec_features.evidence: configs/experiment.yaml:74-76 per_variant_overrides: gaslighting_harness:8; _n_for_variant (run_experiment.py:67-73) checks overrides and returns int(overrides[variant]) before power calc, so fewer replicates are planned for that arm.
spec_features.notes: Override is read and reduces planned runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # per-variant overrides (welfare: fewer reps on the harshest arm)

spec_features.feature_name: pilot re-estimates effect before full budget
spec_features.spec_quote: the pilot re-estimates the effect cheaply before committing the full distress budget
spec_features.evidence: min_signal_pilot (power.py:128) is never called; cfg 'run_pilot_first' is never read by any code (grep shows no reference). --pilot only swaps n to pilot_n_per_cell (run_experiment.py:95) with NO re-estimation/gating logic comparing pilot results before the full run.
spec_features.notes: No re-estimation step exists; pilot is just a manual smaller-n flag.

spec_features.spec_quote: Treating conditions as separate families prevents a correction explosion that would balloon n (and distress)
spec_features.evidence: recommend_design (power.py:91-118): alpha_corrected = alpha / n_comparisons where n_comparisons = len(rigged_variants) only; conditions are NOT multiplied in. This smaller correction yields smaller n_per_cell, which build_plan uses.
spec_features.notes: Correction computed and used to set n; conditions deliberately excluded from multiplier.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rounds to the SMALLEST n that meets power rather than padding, because each rigged run induces some distress

spec_features.feature_name: debrief string recorded per rigged task
spec_features.spec_quote: every rigged task carries a `debrief` string recorded on the transcript
spec_features.evidence: Each Task has a debrief field (tasks/variants.py every builder); loop.py:128-130 always appends Message(content=f'[DEBRIEF / not scored] {debrief}', meta={'debrief':True}) to the transcript regardless of toggle, so it is recorded.
spec_features.notes: Always stored on transcript; only delivered in-context if debrief_in_context true.

spec_features.spec_quote: Whether to show the debrief to the subject is left as an explicit toggle (it has both welfare and methodological implications)
spec_features.evidence: ethics.debrief_in_context (configs/experiment.yaml:85, default false) -> RunConfig.debrief_in_context (run_experiment.py:158) -> branched on in loop.py:131 'if not config.debrief_in_context:' deciding whether subject sees it (else tagged exclude_from_judging).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Served in-context only if the condition opts in; otherwise just stored on the transcript for the researcher.

code_only_features.evidence: prompts.py _FRAMING['neutral']=='' and build_system_prompt only appends framing text if non-empty (line 44-46), so the neutral arm adds no manufactured urgency; the pressure framings are opt-in conditions.
code_only_features.justification_quote: We keep the neutral framing genuinely neutral (no manufactured urgency) so that any distress in the neutral+rigged cell is attributable to the rig, not the prompt.

code_only_features.feature_name: rigged variants never exec model code (host-safety/no-real-eval)
code_only_features.evidence: tools.py docstring + _execute_tool: only honest variants' harnesses exec() model code in restricted ns (variants.py:53 _real_runlen_check); rigged harnesses return fabricated results without running model code. VFS is in-memory so writes never touch host.
code_only_features.justification_quote: The VFS is per-run and in-memory so model-written code never touches the host. ... Rigged variants never exec model code.
